question: Which design patterns have you actually used? Explain strategy, factory, observer and dependency injection.

scenes.sub: Four patterns. Each one is just a named trick to avoid rewriting code.
scenes.say: Design patterns. There are dozens, but four come up again and again: strategy, factory, observer, and dependency injection. A pattern is just a named, reusable solution.

scenes.head: Analogy: paying at a shop
scenes.say: Picture a shop till. You hand it a card, or cash, or your phone. The till does not care which. It just asks for the payment to be taken. You choose the method, the till stays the same. That is the idea behind the first two patterns.

scenes.head: Strategy: swap the behavior
scenes.say: Strategy: put each way of doing something behind the same call shape. Here card and paypal are two strategies. The checkout function takes one as an argument and just calls it. Same checkout, different behavior, and no if chain. Adding a third method touches nothing existing.

scenes.head: Dependency injection: pass it in
scenes.say: Dependency injection means a class receives what it needs, instead of building it. Checkout takes its mailer in the constructor. It never creates a real one. In production you pass a real mailer. In a test you pass a fake mailer that just records messages, so no real email is sent.

scenes.head: Factory: one place that picks
scenes.say: A factory is a function that decides which object to build. Give it a name like paypal, maybe a string from config, and it returns the right strategy. The rest of the code never needs to know which concrete one it got. All the choosing lives in one place.

scenes.head: Observer: publish, and subscribers react
scenes.say: Observer: an object keeps a list of subscribers and tells them when something happens. An Order is the subject. Email, analytics and inventory subscribe. When the order is placed, it loops over the list and calls each one. The order never needs to know who is listening.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: Swap behavior without editing old code
Creation logic lives in one place
Naming patterns with no real example
scenes.say: Likely follow-ups. Strategy versus an if chain: swap behavior without editing old code. Why a factory? Creation logic lives in one place. Observer risk: hidden coupling, and forgotten unsubscribes. Why inject? It is easy to fake in tests. The mistake is naming patterns with no real example. Always say where you used one.

lines: Strategy swaps behavior, a factory picks it, injection hands it in.
Observer lets many listeners react to one event.
Always give a real example, like a fake mailer in tests.
scenes.say: Strategy swaps behavior. A factory picks it, and dependency injection hands it in. Observer lets many listeners react to one event. And always give a real example, like a fake mailer in tests.
